claims.text: HEAs comprise multiple elements in near-equiatomic proportions.
The proposed starting material is an as-deposited nanostructured HEA film composed of multiple transition metals.
The as-deposited HEA has a random elemental distribution.
The as-deposited HEA may have an amorphous or nanocrystalline structure.
Annealing temperature and composition can alter the phase structure and characteristic decomposition length scale of an HEA.
Combinatorial synthesis enables precise compositional tuning of the proposed nanostructured HEA catalyst.
Controlled annealing and composition tuning fine-tune the elemental surface states of the catalyst.
The tailored elemental distribution adjusts the surface d-band state.
Adjusting the d-band center optimizes hydrogen adsorption and desorption energetics.
Optimized hydrogen adsorption and desorption improve the kinetics of HER and HOR.
Multi-element synergistic effects enhance structural stability and corrosion resistance under harsh electrochemical conditions.
Nanostructured, compositionally tuned, annealed HEA catalysts can provide enhanced HER and HOR catalytic activity compared with conventional Pt-based catalysts.
Nanostructured, compositionally tuned, annealed HEA catalysts can provide greater HER and HOR durability than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The tailored HEA catalyst will exhibit lower HER and HOR overpotentials than untreated HEA films and conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The tailored HEA catalyst will exhibit higher HER and HOR current densities than untreated HEA films and conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The tailored HEA catalyst will degrade more slowly during prolonged cycling than untreated HEA films and conventional Pt-based catalysts.
Electrolyte pH, temperature, and potential-cycling protocol may alter the degree of performance enhancement.
Scaling the catalyst to practical device sizes may introduce additional challenges.
